messages:
Emily Chen: FYI — Rate Card v6.1 is scheduled to go live 2026-05-15. This is a minor SKU cleanup: a few legacy per-seat SKUs are being retired and replaced with consolidated usage SKUs. See https://redwood-internal/docs/ratecards/v6-1 for mapping.
Ryan Patel: Thanks Emily. Do we have a mapping table I can paste into SFDC? Some of my deals are mid-commit.
Emily Chen: Yup — linked doc has a CSV mapping. Short summary: old `seat-pro` -> new `usage-pro`, old `seat-lite` -> `usage-lite`. Pricing stays effectively the same, but billing units change to usage tokens.
Sam Torres: Important Q: how does this affect commit crediting? If a customer already committed to X seats, do we convert credits 1:1?
Marta Lopez: We need standard guidance before AEs reprice. If we convert 1:1 some customers will expect the same invoice format. Ops has to handle billing migration.
Emily Chen: Deal Desk/Finance: default conversion is 1:1 for commit accounting for deals signed before 2026-05-15. For new contracts after the effective date, new SKUs apply. Exceptions require Deal Desk approval.
Deal Desk Bot: New exception workflow: submit the 'Rate Card SKU Exception' form -> https://redwood-internal/forms/deal-desk-sku-exception. Include opp ID, signer date, and attach the old quote.
Alex Kim: For POCs: if POC started before cutover but invoice happens after, treat as pre-cutover for crediting. AEs should tag opps with #v6-migration so Deal Desk can batch review.
Ryan Patel: Can we get a canned note I can paste into quotes and CLM? Also, any update to quoting templates?
Emily Chen: We'll push a small quoting template patch tomorrow morning. For now use this snippet in quote notes: "SKU migration: per internal rate card update (v6.1), legacy seat SKUs will map to usage SKUs. Pre-commit deals preserve commit credits; exceptions possible via Deal Desk."
Sam Torres: Does this impact committed volume tiers? E.g., if a customer is at 10k seat credits, do they keep the same tier thresholds?
Emily Chen: Yes — tiers remain intact. Conversion preserves committed units for tiering. Finance confirmed no negative tier movement for pre-cutover commits.
Marta Lopez: OK — Requesting Deal Desk: batch approve exceptions for the next 5 business days for opps tagged `#v6-migration` with signer date <= 2026-05-15. We will provide the CSV export.
Deal Desk Bot: Acknowledged. Please submit the CSV to the form. Ticket will be created per opp and prioritized as "migration".
Alex Kim: One ask from Security/Procurement teams: will the SKU name change break any existing SOW language? Recommend AEs add a clause: "SKU naming changes do not alter pricing or commitments; refer to internal rate card v6.1 mapping."
Ryan Patel: Noted. Will update my SOW template.
Emily Chen: Action items: AEs tag impacted opps with `#v6-migration`; upload CSV to form; quoting templates update goes out tomorrow AM; Deal Desk will batch process for cutoff date. If you have live deals with bespoke terms, loop in @Marta.
Sam Torres: Thanks — can we get a short customer-facing FAQ to answer questions?
Emily Chen: Yes — drafting a 1-pager for AEs + CSMs. Expect it by EOD today.
Alex Kim: Great, thanks. :thumbsup:
Ryan Patel: One more — for ongoing POCs where usage metrics are used for billing, are we changing how we meter?
Emily Chen: No change to metering. Only SKU/billing unit semantics change. Any metering issues — tag eng-billing.
Marta Lopez: Closing note: if anyone finds a deal where the conversion materially changes TCV, escalate to Deal Desk + Finance immediately.
Emily Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone.
